shared_needs: src/theme.css — `.grain > *` (position: relative) has the same specificity as `.screw` (position: absolute) and comes later, so ANY Screw placed inside a .grain container without Tailwind's `absolute` utility collapses to a 0x0 inline box and paints as a small dark square made of its own box-shadow rings. shared_needs: src/components/chrome.tsx — `Well` builds its class list as `well relative ${className}`, so a caller passing `absolute` loses the cascade (both utilities are in the same Tailwind layer and `relative` wins by stylesheet order, not attribute order). The element then keeps `position: relative` while left/right are applied as relative offsets, and it overflows its parent. It cost me two silent 422px-wide overflows on this screen. Suggest `Well` (and any other chrome primitive that hardcodes a positioning utility) accept position through style or drop `relative` when the caller supplies one. I worked around it with inline `position: 'absolute'`.

src/components/chrome.tsx — the shared `.plate` face gradient (#94795e → #866c52 → #78604a → #4a3524) does not match the references. Measured down a row plate in 02-rollcall-rest.jpg, the face is nearly FLAT at #7b5e48 top to bottom with only a bright hairline chamfer at the top edge; the darkness in the reference lives in the gaps BETWEEN plates. I had to overlay a local `PlateGrade` on every plate to pull the top down ~20% and lift the bottom back into the light. Every screen will need the same correction, so the fix belongs in `.plate` in theme.css (or as a graded variant on `Plate`), not repeated per screen. My local `PlateGrade` and `TopSpecular` helpers in RollCall.tsx are the reference implementation if it helps.

src/components/chrome.tsx — `Lamp`'s glow is far wider and softer than the references' sockets, which are crisp filled discs in a brass grommet with falloff inside a few pixels. At 14px in a row, eight rows deep, the halos fogged the plates and contributed materially to the brightness overshoot. I stopped using Lamp for row sockets and hand-rolled a `Socket` (brass ring + inset well / team-coloured emitter with 3px and 7px falloff stops). If the board and team sheet use Lamp at similar sizes, tightening its falloff centrally would help them the same way.

findings.what: The bottom ~60 CSS px of the mounting panel is a dead black void. The reference puts a lit brass ledge there, so in my shot the eight columns stand on nothing and the screen loses its lowest depth layer.
findings.evidence: Measured on the full-width strip below the footing plates: mine (x60-3780, y1990-2110) maxL=44, brightest #322b21, mean #18120d (L≈19). Reference same band (x40-1880, y1000-1055) maxL=213, brightest #e4d2bf, mean #251b15. A vertical scan in mine at x=600 goes L=101 at the footing plate's bottom bevel (y1980) and then never exceeds L=21 from y1984 to the frame edge at y2160. In the reference the equivalent scan at x=300 holds L=56-67 (#44332b–#513e37) with a bright bevel line at L=83 and rust speckle. findings.what: The lit meter does not spill any light onto the footing plate 5px beneath it, at exactly the place the reference makes the spill most obvious.
findings.evidence: Vertical scan in mine at x=300: the bottom lit slot reads #aa49f4 (y1770), and the footing plate's top bevel immediately below reads #eee2c8 (y1800) then #cabba6 — pure warm cream, b<g<r, zero purple cast. The reference at x=150: bottom slot #fd94c6 (y889), then the footing bevel at y919-922 reads #bf7a88 / #c58d94 — visibly pink-cast metal. Confirmed visually in the zoomed footing crops: the reference's plate top edge and the panel around it are washed pink; mine is warm-white.
findings.fix: Give the lit meter a coloured spill onto the metal it borders — tint the footing plate's top bevel and the channel's outer walls with the team colour at tight falloff, the same way the arcs already tint the leader's brass rails teal.

findings.what: The leader's meter channel edges barely glow teal. In the reference they are two bright teal channel rails flanking the slots — one of the strongest reads in the concept.
findings.evidence: src/screens/BigScreen.tsx gives the leader's Well only '0 0 0 1px rgba(47,217,208,0.5), 0 0 22px rgba(47,217,208,0.28)'. Sampled at the channel edge (1970,1300) it is #143735 — a dark teal hairline. The reference at the same relative point shows a wide lit teal band flanking the slot stack (crop crops/ref-meter-edge.jpg: bright cyan vertical rails either side of the red slots, clearly brighter than the slot gaps). Side by side, mine reads as a plain dark channel with two lightning bolts outside it.
findings.fix: Make the channel's own walls emitters on the leader: a 3-4px teal-lit inner rail on both sides of the slot stack with a wider bloom onto the plate, so the current visibly runs through the meter rather than only beside it.

findings.what: The eight footing plates read as polished chrome, not warm bronze — the coolest, brightest elements on the screen.
findings.evidence: Box mean over footing plate 1: mine (70,1810,340x180) = rgb(120,104,87), L≈107; reference (70,905,200x95) = rgb(87,59,56), L≈68. Peak specular is the same in both (236,226,207 vs 246,226,209), so it is the plate body that is too bright and too neutral — mine's face runs #a29078–#d7cdbb across most of its area where the reference's stays #3c2d26–#5c483d with a narrow streak.
findings.fix: Darken the footing plate body toward the reference's bronze and narrow the specular streak so it is a highlight on brass rather than a full-face gradient.

findings.what: No rust patina anywhere on the screen, though the columns pass a `rust` prop. The reference carries it on the footing plates' lower edges, the header plate's lower edge, and the panel band beneath the footings.
findings.evidence: Zoomed footing crops: the reference shows orange oxide along the plate's bottom edge and spreading onto the panel below (#7a4a2a-family speckle), plus rust along the header plate's lower edge. My footing plates and header plate show a clean bevel and no oxide at any edge; the panel below is black.
findings.fix: Emit the rust in the crevices and lower edges that are actually lit — the footing plate's bottom lip and the panel band under it — once that band is lit at all (see the first finding).

findings.what: The leader's bolts read as thick neon zigzag ribbons rather than current: the white-hot core is fat and the teal glow is narrow and hard-edged, the inverse of the reference's proportions.
findings.evidence: Horizontal cross-section through my left bolt at y=1500: two near-white peaks (#e8faf8 L=244 at x1908, #d5f6f4 at x1922) spanning ~24 device px ≈ 12 CSS px of core, wrapped in a hard saturated band (#2ecac1 L=154) with the whole footprint dead by x1880 — ~30 CSS px total. findings.what: The leader carries one stand-off bracket per side; the reference has two per side (top and bottom), with the dark cables running off the lower pair.

findings.what: The hanging key's lowest tooth is a rectangle detached from the shank, and the key's tip clears the medallion bezel by only ~2-3 CSS px, reading as a collision.

findings.what: Gold is used as an arc colour on /display. The reference art does show it, so this is a rule-versus-reference conflict that should be decided rather than passed silently — the report claims a CLAUDE.md 'carve-out' that CLAUDE.md does not contain.

findings.what: A detached grey smoke puff floats ~90px above the hot key, behind the award nameplate, reading as a dirty smudge on the door with nothing connecting it to its source.
findings.evidence: In my shot there is a soft blob centred near device (520,1245) = CSS (260,622): sampled #41352A against the surrounding door at #31261A/#32261C — clearly lighter, ~50px across, sitting between KEY 02 and the TURN TO AWARD plate, with no smoke at all between it and the key at the rail (crop shots/mine-blob.png). In 04-golden-key.jpg the smoke is a continuous thin warm wisp hugging the key, roughly one key-height tall, never detaching and never crossing the type.

findings.what: The hot key's "sparks" are three pale vertical bars rendered inside the bow ring, reading as smears on the key rather than sparks thrown off it.

findings.what: The escutcheon is a plain stadium capsule; the reference focal object is a rectangular plate with an arched top and bottom and square shoulders.

findings.what: The seal legend collides with the bezel screw, and it still runs on the top arc instead of the bottom.

findings.what: On the one screen defined by "no colour but gold", the crest glyph is a saturated salmon-red emitter with a red halo — the loudest colour on the door. The reference crest is warm gold/amber.

findings.what: The coin's specular is a hard-edged detached cream lozenge pasted on the bezel rather than a graded brass highlight.
findings.evidence: shots/sk/coinTL.png at 6x shows a rounded-cap cream bar (sampled #CFBD96 at device 296,205) starting abruptly under the top-left bezel dot and ending in a round cap mid-bezel, with a matching brown bar at lower right. findings.what: Post construction artifacts: a circular seam scar crosses each post face, and the shadowed far-edge strip is drawn on the same edge as the bright inner strip so it protrudes as dark stubs above and below it.
findings.evidence: Crops shots/sk/post.png and post2.png at 5x: an outlined circle cuts visibly across the shaft near each end, and the bright inner strip has a darker offset segment above and below it. Source: the end pads are `r={15}` against `POST_W/2 = 14.5` (so they add only an outline, never a wider foot) and are stroked rgba(24,14,5,0.45); on the left post `inner = px + POST_W` puts the bright rgba(255,214,120,0.55) strip at the same right edge as the rgba(24,14,5,0.4) far-edge strip, which starts 6px higher and ends 6px lower. The reference handles have pads clearly wider than the shaft with their own contact shadow and no seam across the face.
findings.fix: Widen the end pads (r ≈ POST_W/2 + 3) and drop the stroke, and clip or offset the far-edge shadow so it never shares an edge with the inner highlight.

findings.what: The door's inset hairline rule runs straight through all six bolt heads and under the back-button chip, reading as an un-occluded guide line.

findings.fix: Break the hairline around each bolt, or inset it so hardware sits clear of it.

findings.what: The back control is a flat brass chip with no screws and no bevel — out of the screen's own hardware vocabulary, which it states explicitly ("everything operable here is hardware").

src/components/TeamCrest.tsx — the four bezel screws sit at 45°/135°/225°/315° at r=25.4, which is exactly where the 250° legend arc (r=23.4) runs, and both the screw head (#2e2010) and the non-gold legend fill (#33240f) are dark. src/theme.css — `.grain > *` (around line 434) sets `position: relative; z-index: 1` on every direct child, which at equal specificity beats `.screw`'s own `position: absolute; z-index: 2` (line ~265) because it appears later in the sheet. Any `<Screw>` placed as a direct child of a `.grain` element therefore goes static and lands in the layout flow. I worked around it on this screen by passing Tailwind's `absolute` utility through Screw's className, but `BrassPlate` in chrome.tsx has the same latent bug in its `screws` branch. Either scope `.grain > *` (e.g. `.grain > *:not(.screw)`) or give `.screw` `position: absolute !important`.

src/components/chrome.tsx — `Screw` takes `className`, `slot` and `size` but no `style`, so absolute placement has to go through Tailwind arbitrary-value classes. A `style?: CSSProperties` passthrough would be a one-line, non-breaking addition. Also `BrassFrame` renders `CornerScrews` before its children and its children wrapper is `position: relative`, so at band widths under ~11px the interior paints over the inner half of each screw; I ended up passing `screws={false}` and placing my own screws as siblings of the frame.
stats: /#/team/rustco 390x844 dpr2 full: warmth 39.4 · order true · medL 64 · midtone 37.0% · spec 2.33% · mean 81,60,41  —  reference 05-team-sheet.jpg: warmth 44.3 · order true · medL 66 · midtone 37.5% · spec 2.23% · mean 88,64,44 (start of this pass: warmth 33.4 · medL 59 · midtone 33.0% · spec 2.07%; the round-one build measured warmth 35 · medL 97 · midtone 56.1% · spec 1.08%)

findings.what: Nothing on this screen emits light onto its surroundings. Every meter is a lit column with a hard edge and zero spill, so the glow rule ("an emitting source spilling light onto surrounding metal with tight physical falloff") is not satisfied anywhere on the route. The report lists this as merely "tightened"; it is absent.
findings.evidence: Measured on my own shot at DPR2. Row 2 FORGED's lit column at (655,532) is rgb(152,215,113) — a bright green emitter. The plate 8px above it, at (655,506), is rgb(115,93,70). Row 8 RUST CO. at the same x has a DEAD DARK bore, rgb(36,30,25) at (655,1684), and the plate 8px above it at (655,1658) is rgb(116,94,72). The plate above a blazing green tube and the plate above a black one differ by 1/255. Same for INNOCENT: column rgb(242,216,130), plate above rgb(139,113,80) = the ordinary plate value, plate below rgb(95,74,54) = the ordinary bottom-gradient value. In design/reference/05-standings.png every tube floods its plate — the whole plate around the leader's tube reads teal-green and the collars pick up a cool cast.
findings.fix: Give GlassTube a spill layer outside the bore keyed to the fill colour and length — a radial/elliptical gradient painted on the plate under the tube, tightest at the lit column's own extent, dying to transparent within ~10px. It must be drawn outside the bore's overflow clip, or the clip has to go.

findings.what: The leader's teal bolt casts no light on the two brass collars it terminates on, nor on the plate around them. CLAUDE.md: "Arcs cast teal light onto the brown metal and brass they cross." The arc is decoration painted inside a window.
findings.evidence: The leader row's collars are byte-identical to a row with no arc at all. Left collar body sampled at (476,340) in row 1 (arc) = rgb(119,87,40); the same point in row 2 (no arc, y+192) = rgb(119,87,40). Right collar: rgb(119,87,40) in both. Plate 8px left of the left collar: row 1 rgb(127,104,82) vs row 2 rgb(128,105,83). Plate 8px above the tube shifts by only 12/255 in R−B (40 vs 52) and is still solidly warm at rgb(126,110,86). In the reference the plate and both collars around the arc are visibly washed cool.
findings.fix: Composite a teal light pass over the collars and the plate under/around the tube in the leading row only, driven by the same flicker frame as the bolt so it pulses with it. Warm brass under a teal discharge should shift green-grey, not stay rgb(119,87,40).

findings.what: The tube does not read as one cylinder, so its two brass posts read as detached hardware rather than the arc's endpoints. The bore is a pill with a radius equal to half its height; the collars are rounded-rect chips butted against it. At the top and bottom of every tube there is a visible wedge of bare brown plate between the collar's inner face and the glass.
findings.evidence: At 8x on the leader tube and on RUST CO.: the bore's rounded end curves away from the collar so bare plate shows between them for roughly the top and bottom third of the tube's height (~5 CSS px wide at the extremes); only the vertical centreline touches. The lit column is consequently a bar floating inside a black lozenge with its own ends clipped into lens shapes. The reference glass is a straight barrel with two specular rails along it that visibly continues BEHIND both collars, and each end holds a bright metal electrode on which the arc root explodes white-hot — ours has no electrode and the strands just fade into the rounded end.
findings.fix: Draw the bore full-width (no collar inset) with a small radius and paint the collars on top of it, and add an electrode plug inside each end for the arc to root on. This is the `boreOverlap` item already noted in the report's shared_needs — it is visible at 1x, not a nicety.

findings.what: Numerals are not actually tabular. Oswald ships no `tnum` feature, so `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is inert. The scores share a right edge but their digit stems and decimal points do not line up down the column — which is the whole point of the rule.
findings.evidence: From the live DOM at 390px, the eight 28px scores all end at right=356 but measure: 15.9 → 48.4px wide, 15.3 → 47.7, 14.3 → 48.1, 12.8 → 48.1, 11.8 → 44.7, 11.7 → 42.2, 11.5 → 44.3. 12.8 and 11.7 have identical glyph counts and differ by 5.9px, so their leading "1"s start at 307.9 vs 313.8 and their decimal points sit ~2.5px apart. CLAUDE.md requires "Tabular numerals, right-aligned, sharing a column edge."
findings.fix: Either set the numeral column in JetBrains Mono (which is monospaced by construction), or hand-set each glyph in a fixed-width cell so the decimal point is positionally locked. Declaring tabular-nums on Oswald does nothing.

findings.what: INNOCENT's golden key is invisible in its meter, and RUST CO. — which has zero keys — appears to have a gold cap. The key/base distinction the tube is supposed to encode fails on two of eight rows.
findings.evidence: At 8x, INNOCENT's fill is one unbroken yellow-gold ramp from collar to meniscus with no perceptible boundary, because the team token #FFD84D and the key gold #FFC63D are ~0.02 apart in hue; its readout says +1.0 of key but the tube shows none. On RUST CO. (+0.0 keys) the fill terminates in a hard pale bar measured at rgb(254,227,165) — the same cream-gold used as the key/meniscus colour elsewhere — so a keyless team's tube ends in what reads as a gold key segment. That pale bar also overhangs the lit column vertically by 1–2px on both edges.
findings.fix: Separate the key continuation from the base fill with a dark hairline gap or a notch rather than a colour change, so it survives INNOCENT's yellow; and drop or restyle the meniscus so it cannot be mistaken for the key cap on zero-key rows.

findings.what: The rank well is a flat black hole, not a machined recess, and the reference's brass rank ring is missing entirely.
findings.evidence: Horizontal scan across the row-3 rank well at y=666: plate L=130 steps in ONE pixel to L=17, then a dead-flat rgb(22,15,12) for 72px, then steps back in one pixel. Vertically (x=90) the interior runs L=4 at the top to L=17 and holds flat — no `--well-rim` hairline on the bottom-right lip, no bevel, no ring. REFERENCE-SPEC part 4 requires inner shadow darkest at the top-left lip plus one `--well-rim` hairline bottom-right; in design/reference/05-standings.png the rank numeral sits inside a raised brass annulus within its own bracketed sub-panel, which we do not have at all.
findings.fix: Rebuild the rank as the Recess part with a real inner shadow and a bottom-right rim hairline, and put a brass ring around it so it reads as turned hardware instead of a punched hole.

findings.what: The wall behind the hardware carries no material texture, and there is no rust patina anywhere on the screen — not in a crevice, not along a lower edge.

At 10x zoom our plate faces and medallion interiors are smooth airbrushed gradients; every reference plate frame and screw seat is rusted and grained.

The overall material stats are already calibrated (warmth 29.8 / medL 58 / midtone 37.3 / spec 2.28 sits inside the v2 band of 30.9–44.3 / 64–66 / 37.5–39 / 2.23–2.46), so this is texture, not tone.

findings.what: The medallion is about two thirds of its reference relative size and its interior is a flat gradient, so the row's visual anchor is the black rank hole instead of the crest.

findings.what: The activity lamps' glow is clipped by the well's border, and the glow language on this screen is inconsistent — these lamps bloom generously while the meters, the brightest emitters present, bloom not at all.

findings.what: Technical labels are set at 8px and 7px, below a usable floor on a 390px phone.

findings.what: The 6/7 punctuality cliff is not surfaced at all — 6/7 and 7/7 rows are pixel-identical in any still frame, and identical even in motion under prefers-reduced-motion.

'pulse-rim' : ''}` — and theme.css:594-606 makes pulse-rim nothing but `opacity: 0.3 -> 1`, applied to the whole knob, so at 6/7 the seventh control periodically fades to a 30% ghost (reads as disabled, not "rimmed amber and pulsing"). theme.css:642-647 sets `animation: none` under prefers-reduced-motion; I re-ran the board with reducedMotion:'reduce' and the computed opacity of the 6/7 wrapper is "1" — byte-identical to the 7/7 row. CLAUDE.md: "Surface that tension: at 6/7 the seventh socket is rimmed and pulsing" and "Honor prefers-reduced-motion: keep state changes."

findings.what: The binary-cell glow repaints the plate face across the whole row in the team colour — measurably, in every row. It is not tight-falloff motivated light, it is a wash, and two rows end up with a non-warm plate face.
findings.evidence: I sampled the identical strip of plate face just below the recessed channel (dpr2 x 480-640, plate top + 37 CSS) in all eight rows of my screenshot and computed B-G (a neutral warm brass sits near -25, confirmed by the footer plate control at #8b7359, B-G -25.5): WARRIORS #986463 (B-G -0.7, rose), PRECIOUS #875f71 (B-G +18.0, violet — a 43-point swing off the control), GEMS #726d6a (B-G -3.4, R-G +5, i.e. neutral grey), KNIGHTS #93604a (-22), FORGED #7c7c46 (-53.8, olive), INNOCENT #92774c (-43.2). At 5x (shots/zz-cells.png) the pink halo covers the entire channel interior and continues onto the plate face below and to the right of it. In the reference at the same 3x (shots/zz-refcells.png) the cells are flat, crisp, uniform saturated pink squares in warm-rimmed sockets with effectively zero spill — the channel stays dark brown between adjacent cells and the plate face outside the channel is the same brass in every row. CLAUDE.md: "Never apply glow as decoration... tight physical falloff" and "If a screenshot reads blue-grey, it is wrong" — the GEMS row's plate face is now neutral grey and PRECIOUS's is violet.
findings.fix: Cut Lamp's spill radius hard for the board (the reported `spill` multiplier idea, at roughly 0.3-0.5, not 0.6) and clip the glow to the channel so it cannot reach the plate face at all. Separately, the lit cell needs a crisp 1px rim and a hard edge, not a blurred square.

findings.what: Each lit binary cell has a yellow-white amber core inside the team-colour square, so the same amber lamp shows through pink, purple, blue, green and yellow glass.

The reference cell (shots/zz-refcells.png) is a flat, evenly-filled pink square with at most a marginally lighter inner face of the same hue and no lighter core of any other colour. REFERENCE-SPEC line 115: "Earned: a filled glowing square in the team color with a bright inner face."

findings.what: Plate faces are ~40 L too bright and fall outside the band the spec's own definition of done mandates; the header is worse and reads pale khaki rather than bronze.

Region means: build header inner panel #bba37c L165.1 vs reference #846d57 L112.0; build header overall mean L138.0 vs reference L96.8, with median hue 36.6deg (yellow-khaki) against the reference's 28.5deg (bronze). Your own report frames this as a shared theme.css item, but on this screen the header is 53 L points over the reference, not a rounding error.

findings.what: The rank chip is a near-black cutout where the reference is a shallow machined recess in brass — an 18x luminance error, repeated eight times.

At 6x/8x side by side (shots/zz-refrowscrew.png vs shots/zz-browscrew.png) the reference chip is plainly the plate's own brown, sunk, with a dark inner shadow along the top-left lip and a bright cream rim along the bottom-right; the build's chip is an opaque black rounded rectangle that reads as an LCD window. The reference reserves the dark window for the score readout only — reference score well interior #1d1510 L22.6 (clean sample, min 20 max 24) vs the build's #0e0c0b L12.4.
findings.fix: Stop using the same `Well` for the rank chip. Give it a recess whose floor is the plate colour darkened ~15%, with the inner shadow at the top-left and a --well-rim hairline at the bottom-right. Separately lift the score well's floor from L12 to L23 (#1d1510).

findings.what: There is no rust patina anywhere on the screen. The reference's most prominent single texture — orange oxide across the right two-thirds of the footer — is absent.
findings.evidence: Rust-hue census (hue 5-26deg, S>0.42, L 35-140) on matched regions: footer right — reference 26.19% of pixels vs build 0.52%; header — reference 2.60% vs build 0.00%; row-1 plate face — reference 8.04% vs build 2.32%. Visually confirmed at 1.45x: the reference footer (shots/zz-reffooter.png) carries clear orange-brown mottling from mid-plate rightward and the header's right end has rust streaks; my footer crop (shots/zz-footer.png) is uniform khaki with none. Both CLAUDE.md and REFERENCE-SPEC line 89 require "rust patina in crevices and along lower edges."
findings.fix: Put oxide decals on the footer plate's right half and along the lower edges/corners of the header frame and the row plates, in the reference's hue band (roughly 5-26deg, S>0.42, L 35-130). Keep it to crevices and lower edges — do not wash the plate.

findings.what: The key rail invents a bright brass bar with J-hooks, and it is the brightest object in the row. The reference has no bar, hangs full keys, and draws a dark key silhouette in every empty slot.
findings.evidence: At 6x (shots/build-keys.png) I see a pale brass bar (L~200, brighter than any plate or key) sitting outside the capsule — its top edge is above the capsule's top rim (Board.tsx:343, `top: -3`) and its two rivet ends protrude past the pill's left and right edges onto the plate face — carrying three small J-hooks with one small key, whose teeth cross below the capsule's bottom rim. At 3.5x the reference (shots/refkeys.png) has a narrow pill slot with no bar at all: two full-size lit gold keys and one full dark key silhouette, bows overhanging the slot's top lip, and nothing in the capsule out-glows the keys.
findings.fix: Remove the rail bar from the board variant (or drop its top stop to ~#a8823c so it cannot out-glow gold), remove the `lit &&` guard so empty capacity draws the dark key silhouette instead of a hook, and shrink the capsule to the reference's narrow slot so the key bodies overhang it rather than being clipped by it.

findings.what: Rank chips read 01, 02, 03, 03, 05, 06, 07, 08 — duplicated 03 and no 04 anywhere on the board. This is the exact defect the spec calls out as already-wrong.
findings.evidence: DOM text of the eight chips: ["01","02","03","03","05","06","07","08"], visible in my screenshot as two adjacent rows both stamped 03 (GEMS 6.0 and FORGED 6.0). The reference reads 01 through 08 with no repeats. REFERENCE-SPEC line 110-111: "Rank chip — a recessed square well with a light border, `01`..`08` in cream tabular numerals. Sequential and correct; the build had duplicates." Nothing in the repo records competition ranking being accepted as an override, and the spec text is unambiguous. A board with no rank 04 on it reads as a bug to the camp director, not as a tie.
findings.fix: Render the row's position (1..8, always sequential) in the chip. If shared standing matters, express the tie some other way — a hairline tie bracket between the two rows, or an equals mark beside the score — and leave the chip strictly 01-08.

findings.what: Lit punctuality sockets show no brass collar and no bore — they are bare amber domes. Your report claims the opposite was fixed.

findings.what: Fasteners are roughly 3x the reference's diameter, and the header's engraved frame lines are drawn straight across three of them.

Build row-plate screw head 25 source = 12.5 CSS; reference row-plate rivet 12 source = 4.3 CSS (shots/zz-refrowscrew.png shows a small domed brass rivet flush on the plate, no dark washer, no slot). findings.what: The day rail's past-day socket carries a pale cream horizontal bar across its face that reads as a minus sign, and no socket has the reference's four notches.

The reference socket (shots/ref-rail2.png) is a brass ring with four dark notch slots at N/E/S/W and a clean recessed face; the lit one glows teal through the face and the notches; the future ones keep the brass collar over a dark bronze face. findings.what: The row grid is off the 8px grid the spec and CLAUDE.md both demand, with fractional sub-pixel pitches.

Build status line reads "STATUS: ONLINE / SYNC: 98% / VER: 2.2.1"; the reference reads "STATUS: ONLINE / SYNC: 98% / VER: 2.2.1 / ID: 987R 60H0" (REFERENCE-SPEC line 126).
findings.fix: Widen the barcode to ~141x15 with finer, more varied bars and append the `/ ID: …` segment to the mono line.

findings.what: The commit discharge does not light the row stack at all. The report's claim of "teal light filling the wall gaps above" is false — the rows are pixel-identical between rest and commit.
findings.evidence: I captured the seated frame myself (click ALL, pointer-drag the slider to y=830, screenshot while held → refute-commit.png; the frame is genuinely seated: white socket, 0.5/0.4 readouts, teal-flooded housing, "RELEASE TO COMMIT"). Rows 1–5 band (x30..750, y288..800) measures meanRGB #645140, L p50 89, p95 146, max 217 in BOTH the rest and the commit frame — identical to every digit. The wall gap below row 8 (x100..680, y1172..1184) is #0E0906 / L p50 10 / max 13 in BOTH frames. Reference: the same rows band goes #6F5644 → #755948, p95 192 → 219, max 250 → 255 (02 → 03), and the gap below row 8 goes #241710 (L 27) → #595345 (L 86) with blue lifted 16 → 69. The only thing that changes outside the housing in the build is row 8's bottom edge, #5C452F → #684A2F — red 92→104, green 69→74, blue 47→47, i.e. a WARM lift, the opposite of teal.
findings.fix: The discharge spill element in RollCall.tsx (~line 605) is confined to the housing. Give it enough height/blur to reach the row stack and let it tint the wall in every gutter, with a teal-biased colour so blue actually rises. REFERENCE-SPEC 03: "teal light spills up onto the row plates above."

findings.what: The tube has no white-hot core in either state — no blowout on commit, no white filament at rest.
findings.evidence: Commit tube core (build x300..500,y1390..1470) = mean #508982, L p50 117, p95 186, max 209 — it never reaches 255 anywhere. Reference 03's core (x420..720,y1470..1620) = mean #9EEBE5, L p50 216, p95 255, p99 255, max 255: over a quarter of that rect is fully blown out. At rest, reference 02's tube filament peaks at #ACF8F4 (L 247, p99 236) while the build's whole tube rect maxes at L 112 (p99 98). The build's resting tube also reads darker than the glass: interior mean #28261C (L≈38) vs the reference's #464C43 (L≈73), so it looks like a black slot with a dim scribble rather than lit glass.
findings.fix: CLAUDE.md requires two layers: "thin white-hot core path + thicker teal glow beneath". Add a genuine #FFFFFF core stroke to the arc path (and a saturated blowout sprite at the bore centre on commit), and lift the tube's glass interior so the housing plate reads through it.

findings.what: The 6/7 punctuality cliff is not surfaced anywhere on the screen, contradicting the report's "amber pulsing rim at 6/7".
findings.evidence: Two teams sit at the cliff — aria-labels read "Precious Pieces, 6 of 7 check-ins, already logged" and "Fire Knights, 6 of 7 check-ins, already logged". Both are `disabled`, and RollCall.tsx:535 gates the rim on `!on && !done && ticks === 6`, so it never renders. Measured: PRECIOUS's 7th socket ring is #A38354 and KNIGHTS' is #A48253 — indistinguishable from PEARLS' two ordinary unlit sockets at #A38253, and actually dimmer than RUST CO.'s unlit rings. No amber (#ED9040) anywhere near them, no rim, no pulse. document.body.innerText for the whole page is "PUNCTUALITY / LUNCH · 13:00 / WARRIORS … RUST CO. / ALL / 2 OPEN / PULL TO COMMIT" — there is no "0.6", no "1.0", no "→".
findings.fix: CLAUDE.md: "at 6/7 the seventh socket is rimmed and pulsing and the readout previews 0.6 → 1.0." Drop `!done` from the cliffRim condition (a logged 6/7 row is precisely the one whose seventh check-in is still at risk) and surface the 0.6 → 1.0 preview on the row, not only on the knob after selection.

findings.what: The cog knob is a different part from the reference's, has no light direction, and geometrically collides with the row's right-hand corner screws.
findings.evidence: 5× crops side by side. Reference: a raised brass gear — a thick bright annulus with sculpted teeth each individually lit from the top left, a recessed dark centre well, and a raised bright brass 8-point star inside the well. Build: a flat tan disc ringed by hard black-and-tan rectangular dashes of identical value at top-left and bottom-right (a dashed stroke, no light direction at all), two glassy crescent shines, and a DARK engraved 8-spoke glyph on a light face — contrast inverted from the reference's bright star in a dark recess, and no recessed centre. Collision: the knob spans x 641–733 (DPR2) while the right corner screws span x 716–743 — 17px of overlap (8.5 CSS px); in the reference the knob clears the screws with a clear brass margin.
findings.fix: Rebuild CogKnob as three layers (toothed brass annulus lit top-left / dark inner recess / raised bright star or cream numeral inside it) and shrink it or widen the plate's right padding so it stops overlapping the screws.

findings.what: The tick gauges do not ignite on commit, and they are detached from the rails.
findings.evidence: Left tick column, same rect in each frame: build goes L p95 79 → 158, max 94 → 190 with the ignited column's mean colour #60523B (brass brown). Reference 02→03 goes L p95 71 → 244, max 129 → 251 — nearly half the ignited column reads as near-white amber. Position: in reference 02/03 the ticks are engraved down the vertical brass guide rails themselves; in the build they float on the housing wall well outboard of the rails, so nothing about them reads as part of the mechanism.
findings.fix: REFERENCE-SPEC 02: "Two vertical brass rails … with engraved tick gauges down the outer side of each" and 03: "the tick gauges ignite amber". Move the tick columns onto the rails and drive them to --color-lamp-hot (#FEDF97) on discharge.

findings.what: Plate and brass specular are systematically missing and read neutral grey rather than warm brass — the flatness tell.
findings.evidence: Row-2 top chamfer band: reference (x140..990,y372..380) mean #987A63, L p95 192 / p99 224 / max 232. Build (x60..740,y288..298) mean #726250, L p95 146 / p99 166 / max 172 — the build's brightest chamfer pixel sits below the reference's 95th percentile. Warmth of the highlight itself: reference R−B 53, build R−B 34; the header plate's top chamfer samples #AB9C89 (nearly neutral) against the reference's #9A7D66 rising to #FBD7B7. Lever housing: build max L 213 vs reference 251 — --plate-spec #FFEED3, --brass-spec #FBE1B7 and --knurl-spec #FFEEC2 appear nowhere on this screen. (Plate FACE luminance is fine: build 84–96 vs reference 78–98, so this is purely the highlight, not the base.)
findings.fix: Push the 2px top-left chamfer to --plate-spec / --brass-spec at full value rather than a mid-brass tint, and give the brass parts a real peak highlight. The base plates don't need to move.

findings.what: The lever footing is missing the reference's cast-brass modelling, and the housing has no bottom corner screws.
findings.evidence: 2.4× crops. Reference footing: a stepped brass yoke base (raised where the rails land, dipping in the middle), bright specular streak along the top, and a RECESSED engraved nameplate with chamfered corners and a rivet at each end. Build: one slab split into three abutting panels with two visible vertical seams, the caption sitting on the middle panel with no nameplate border and no rivets, and the rail-end collars floating behind it rather than landing on it. Bottom corner screws: reference bottom-left corner rect (x80..140,y1830..1890) reads L p99 110 / max 223 — a bright brass screw head; the build's equivalent (x30..70,y1620..1670) reads L p99 53 / max 63 — nothing there. The build's housing has screws at the top two corners only. There is also zero rust patina in the build's housing where the reference has heavy rust down both guides and across the lower plate.
findings.fix: REFERENCE-SPEC definition of done: "Screws, bevels, recesses and specular highlights are present on every plate." Add the two bottom screws, make the footing one stepped casting with a recessed riveted nameplate, and add rust in the housing's lower crevices.

findings.what: A black status letterbox across the top of the lever housing that exists in neither reference and reads as a debug HUD.
findings.evidence: Build shows a flat near-black horizontal band spanning the housing with a brass "ALL" tab at the left and right-aligned mono "2 OPEN"; on commit it becomes "CLEAR" / "2 TEAMS QUEUED". It has no bevel, no brass frame and no inner-shadow rim, unlike every other recess on the screen (the LCD window, the sockets). Neither 02 nor 03 has anything in that position — the reference housing goes straight from its top corner screws to the grip's travel. Also on commit the footing caption changes to "RELEASE TO COMMIT" where reference 03 still reads "PULL TO COMMIT".
findings.fix: If the queued/committed counts must stay, cut them into a properly modelled recess (inner shadow at the top-left lip, --well-rim hairline bottom-right, thin brass frame) sized like the LCD window, or move them off the machine entirely. Keep the footing caption stable.

findings.what: Header plate carries three controls the reference plate does not, the back chevron overlaps two corner screws, and the activity steppers are 10px-tall tap targets.
findings.evidence: DOM rects: back "Back to board" [27,32,22,22], "Previous activity" [341,32,22,10], "Next activity" [341,44,22,10]. A 5× crop of the top-left corner shows the chevron plate visibly occluding the lower-right edge of the upper screw and the upper-right edge of the lower screw. Reference 02/03 header plate holds the LCD window and four unobstructed corner screws and nothing else. The steppers are 10px tall on a 12px pitch — off the 8px grid and unusable with a finger on a 390px phone.
findings.fix: Move the chevron and steppers off the screw inset (or out of the header plate into the bezel), and give the steppers at least a 24px hit box each.

findings.what: The punctuality socket track is roughly half the reference's relative weight, so each row is a small dotted strip inside a tall empty plate.
findings.evidence: Reference socket outer diameter 45px / 2.738 px-per-CSS = 16.4 CSS on a 41 CSS row = 40% of row height, pitch 22.6 CSS. Build: 27px / 2 = 13.5 CSS on a 56 CSS row = 24% of row height, pitch 18 CSS. Visible in the matched row crops: in the reference the seven sockets are the row's dominant band; in the build there are wide empty brass bands above and below them. This — not "structural frame height" as the report argues — is why the machine covers less of the frame.
findings.fix: Either bring rows to ~44–48px or scale the sockets up to ~17px with a 22px pitch so the track carries the row the way it does in the reference.

findings.what: On commit only one socket goes white-hot, and the knob readout is dark-on-light where the reference is cream-on-dark.
findings.evidence: Build INNOCENT reads 4 amber + 1 white + 2 dark; RUST CO. reads 3 orange + 1 white + 3 dark (wholeTrackHot is gated on ticks+1===7 at RollCall.tsx:460). Reference 03 turns the whole remaining track white: MYSTIC CIRCLE 5 white, FOREST STALKER 1 green + 4 white, TECHNO FORGE 1 green + 4 white. The build's readouts (0.5, 0.4) are dark brown numerals on the pale knob face; reference 03's 1.0 is large cream inside the knob's dark recessed centre.
findings.fix: Light the whole pull-adds range white-hot, and put the readout as cream in the knob's recess. (The values themselves are correct integer tenths.)

findings.what: Medallion bezel loses its lower rim light and the crest is a solid fill rather than the reference's line art in a glossy dome.
findings.evidence: Vertical scan through the bezel: build top #AC8250 (L 133) → bottom #37251C (L 40), i.e. the lower bezel goes essentially black. Reference: top #B69571 (L 152) → bottom #8A7353 (L 115) — a full brass torus with a bounce along the bottom. The build shows two bezel dots where REFERENCE-SPEC calls for four at the diagonals, and the glyph is a solid filled diamond over a flat purple field where the reference is a luminous line-art crest over a glossy domed interior with a top specular.
findings.fix: Keep --well-rim-level bounce on the bezel's lower-right arc, add the missing two bezel screws, and switch the crest to line art on a domed interior.

findings.what: LCD window interior is half the reference's brightness and is still ringed by a saturated amber hairline.
findings.evidence: Vertical scan through the window: build interior runs #0C0806 → #241A12, median ≈ #1E150F (L 23), framed by a 2px #8A6A33 keyline. Reference interior is a consistent #3D2C24–#423127 (L ≈ 50) inside a ~6px modelled brass band with rust patina, i.e. more than twice as bright. The report claims the "bright orange ring on pure black" was replaced; measured, the ring is still a saturated 2px orange line against a near-black field.
findings.fix: Lift the window interior toward the reference's #3F2E25 and replace the keyline with a modelled brass band (lit top-left, --brass-lo bottom-right) so it reads as a frame rather than a stroke.

findings.what: The team seal — the largest object on the screen — is a glowing orange lamp where the reference is a brushed-gold coin. Its material, its emblem drawing and its light hierarchy are all different.
findings.evidence: Cropped both seals at matching scale. Reference: the coin face is bright radial-brushed gold (sampled 236,212,160 on the ring specular; 196,165,109 on the ring body), with a raised rust-orange gear+flame+wrench emblem carrying gold specular edges on top of it, and the legend RUST REVIVAL CO. engraved DARK into the bright gold ring — every letter legible, high contrast, and the whole legend sits on the coin. Build: the interior is a dark brown well filled by a flat orange radial bloom with a crude ring of 12 rounded-rectangle 'teeth' and a plain orange disc plus a dark centre dot — it reads as a lit fan or a vent lamp, not an emblem. There is no flame, no wrench, no gear silhouette. Sampled the interior at 420,110 = (169,98,42) glowing orange against a dark well. The result is that the brightest, highest-chroma object on the whole screen is the coin's interior, whereas in the reference the coin is metal and the brightest cream is the total numeral — the hierarchy is inverted.
findings.fix: Give TeamCrest's seal case (label set) a warm radial brushed-brass interior in the --brass-hi/--brass band, and put the team colour only into a raised emblem drawn on top of it with a gold specular edge and a tight local bloom, not a full-disc glow. Redraw the emblem as a layered silhouette (gear ring behind, flame/wrench in front) rather than a ring of blocks.

findings.what: The seal's circular legend is dark-on-dark and collides with the header frame's brass band; part of it is eaten by a bezel screw.
findings.evidence: In my screenshot the legend arc's baseline crosses the header frame's pale top band (band at y≈22–37 CSS; the letters RUST and CO. sit on and over it), so the type straddles two materials with a hard edge running through the letterforms. Sampled the legend fill area at 330,105 = (59,34,14) against a wall/ring of (101,71,48) and a band of (152,120,62) — the type is darker than both grounds but only by ~L20 against the ring, so at 390px it reads as smudge, not engraving. The top-left bezel screw sits directly on the leading R. The reference legend is dark engraving on an L~170–210 gold ring with nothing crossing it.
findings.fix: Put the legend on the coin's own bright brass ring (raise the ring luminance under the type) so the whole arc sits clear of the frame band, and move the bezel screws to 0/90/180/270 or out to r≈27.5 so they never land under the 250° legend arc.

findings.what: Every plate's top chamfer is a blown-out near-white pinstripe in discontinuous flat segments — desaturated, ~85 L units brighter than the reference, and encoding no light direction.
findings.evidence: Scanned the cleanliness plate's top lip across x. Build (y=523): L136, 236, 236, 236, 179, 155, 156, 239, 239, 239, 188, 112, 154, 198, 197 — i.e. flat blocks of rgb(246,239,221) with abrupt steps down to L112–198 between them, and R−B of only 26 (near-neutral white). Reference (y=689): L123, 125, 127, 140, 152, 155, 139, 132, 127, 120 — a smooth warm swell, peak rgb(188,149,115), R−B 64–73. So the build's specular is both blown out and cold, and its bright/dark segments do not decay from the top-left; the brightest patch on the cleanliness plate is at x≈250 CSS, not at the left end.
findings.fix: Cap the chamfer highlight near --plate-spec-in-context (L ~150–160), warm it to R−B ≈ 65, widen it to ~3–4px, and make its intensity decay monotonically away from the plate's top-left corner instead of alternating in blocks.

findings.what: The ON toggle does not emit. It has no recessed seat and almost no bloom spilling onto the plate, so the emissive amber track reads as a flat painted capsule.
findings.evidence: Measured the plate immediately left of a capsule on an ON row against the same point on an OFF row, at the same offset within the row. Reference: ON-row plate at (830,1105) = (107,66,35) L72, R−B 72; OFF-row plate at (830,1435) = (70,53,40) L56, R−B 30 — a +16 L, +42 warmth lift from the lamp. Build: ON-row plate at (590,878) = (113,78,52) L84, R−B 61; OFF-row plate at (590,582) = (105,74,51) L79, R−B 54 — only +5 L, +7 warmth. The 3.4× crop also shows the build capsule is a single flat tan hairline ring over an orange gradient, with no recessed seat, no dark top-left inner shadow and no lit lower-right lip, and the knob is a flat khaki-olive sphere (~#b5ad7e) fully inside the track with no cast shadow, where the reference knob is a machined brass cylinder standing proud of the capsule with a hard shadow beneath it.
findings.fix: Add the outer recessed seat (inner shadow top-left, --well-rim hairline bottom-right), thicken the brass bezel to ~3px with its own bevel, add a real box-shadow spill onto the plate sized to match the reference's +16 L / +42 warmth lift, and make the knob a vertically-brushed brass cylinder that overhangs the track with a contact shadow.

findings.what: The punctuality lamps are plain filled amber balls overflowing a barely-visible trough, not brass-bezel sockets in a recessed channel; and the 6/7 cliff renders as four detached orange dashes floating beside the cog instead of the cog's rim burning.
findings.evidence: Compared the reference charge track to the build's at 2.2×, and shot /#/team/knights (seed day 1 = 6 ticks) to get the cliff state. Reference: each lamp is a brass bezel ring around a dark well with a small amber core, lamps clearly separated, sitting inside a channel whose brass floor is visible above and below them; the seventh is a heavy ornate annulus with rosette engraving and a continuous amber halo hugging its rim, light spilling onto the plate. Build: the lamps are solid amber spheres with only a thin dark rim, touching each other with no gaps, and they break above and below the dark trough so the well is visible only as a shadow to the left of lamp 1 — the recess reads as a crescent behind the first ball. The seventh cog is a plain brass ring with 8 rivet dots and no rosette, and at 6/7 the cliff is four short thick orange arc segments sitting OUTSIDE the cog with a visible gap between them and the metal — they read as stray dashes on the plate, not as a burning rim.
findings.fix: Draw each lamp as bezel + dark well + small amber core with ~4px gaps, shrink them so the channel's brass floor shows above and below, and replace the four detached arcs with a continuous rim glow drawn on the cog's own annulus plus a spill onto the plate.

findings.what: The key rail's six hooks are flat dark-brown J-hooks dangling below the bar. The reference has no such object — its hooks are brass tongues seated flush in milled slots on the bar face.
findings.evidence: Cropped both rails. Reference: six rounded-rectangle brass tongues sitting in dark milled slots within the bar's own height; nothing hangs below the bar except the keys. Build: six dark brown J-shaped coat hooks protruding ~35 CSS px below the bar, rendered as flat silhouettes with no bevel, no specular, no brushing and no contact shadow — they are the flattest objects on the screen and they sit against the wall, not on the bar.
findings.fix: Replace the dangling J-hooks with the reference's flush brass tongues in recessed slots (dark milled slot, brass tongue with a top-left lit edge), and hang the keys from the tongues.

findings.what: On the default load of this route the `+ KEY` tab — the reference's brightest cream element, and per CLAUDE.md the most important object in the app — renders as a dead grey-brown slab less than half the luminance of the bar it is attached to, and is disabled so it is not operable at all.
findings.evidence: DOM: the +KEY button is `disabled: true, aria-disabled: "true"` on /#/team/rustco with no seeding. Sampled the tab face at (650,1400) = (79,65,41) L66 against the same rail bar at (300,1400) = (179,135,62) L139 — the tab is L66 vs the bar's L139, a different and colder material. The label computes to cream rgb(237,227,210) but renders mid-grey through opacity. Reference: the tab is continuous with the bar (sampled 190,161,112 / 127,91,57 — same brass as the bar's 125,100,60) and `+ KEY` is bright cream heavy condensed.
findings.fix: Either don't gate the key tab on this route by default, or give the gated state a legible cold-brass treatment that still keeps the tab's material continuous with the bar; the current opacity knockdown makes the screen's primary action read as broken.

findings.what: The seven punctuality check-in buttons overlap each other by 4–5px, so tapping a socket's right edge fires the next activity.
findings.evidence: DOM bounding boxes: lefts 215.2, 233.2, 251.1, 269, 287, 304.9, 335.2 with width 22 each. 215.2 + 22 = 237.2 > 233.2, and the same for every consecutive pair. aria-labels are per-activity ("Morning exercise 08:30", "Breakfast 09:00", …), so the overlap means the last-painted button wins and the wrong activity gets recorded. The buttons are also 22×40, under the 44px minimum.
findings.fix: Set each button's width to the socket pitch minus a gap (≤17px) or use a single row-wide control that maps x to a socket index, and enlarge the vertical hit area to 44px.

findings.what: Three of the six category glyphs read as a different object than the reference's.
findings.evidence: Side by side at matching scale. Good Deed — reference: an unmistakable three-quarter handshake, two hands clasped with visible fingers and cuffs. Build: two rectangles flanking a fist blob on a horizontal axis; it reads as a belt with a buckle or a dumbbell. Lesson Knowledge — reference: a brain in profile with a brainstem, circuit traces and round solder nodes. Build: a cloud/flower blob containing three wiggly worms, no profile, no stem, no nodes; it reads as a cauliflower. Behavior — reference: a hero standing square, hands on hips, cape flaring right. Build: a thin forward-leaning walking figure whose head is a detached circle with a visible gap above the shoulders, and no cape — it reads as a pedestrian-crossing pictogram, at a visibly thinner stroke weight than the other five glyphs.
findings.fix: Redraw the handshake with two interlocking hands and visible fingers; add a brain profile silhouette + stem + terminal node dots; give the behavior figure a joined head, planted stance and an actual cape, at the same 2.9px stroke as the rest of the set.

findings.what: The hung key's bloom is banded into three hard-edged concentric rings instead of a smooth falloff.
findings.evidence: On /#/team/knights (1 key) at 2.6× the key bow is surrounded by three visibly discrete concentric discs with hard boundaries, plus a second banded set around the shaft. The reference's two keys carry a single smooth continuous gold bloom with no visible steps.
findings.fix: Replace the four-stop radial with a many-stop or blurred layer so no stop boundary is visible at 2× — the banding is the classic ramp-with-too-few-stops artifact.

findings.what: About 116px — 14% of the viewport — of bare wall sits below the key rail, and the report understates it as "roughly 60px".
findings.evidence: DOM: rail bar 689→718, hook tips measured at y≈728 in the screenshot (px 1457 of 1688), document height 844. That is 116 CSS px of empty wall with nothing in it on /#/team/rustco (79px on /knights where a key hangs to ≈765). In the reference the rail is the last element and the keys reach within ~30 CSS px of the image's bottom edge.
findings.fix: Either grow the rail/rows to consume the remaining height or dock the rail to the bottom safe area so the composition closes the way the reference does.

findings.what: The back button's 44×44 hit box is positioned a quarter off-canvas, and the day tabs are 20px tall on a 37px off-grid pitch.
findings.evidence: DOM: the Back button is at top -6, left -6, 44×44 — 6px of it is outside the viewport on both axes, leaving ~38×38 reachable. Day tabs are 30×20 at lefts 106, 143, 180, 217, 254 — a 37px pitch with 7px gaps, neither a multiple of 8, and 20px tall against the project's 8px-grid and tap-target discipline.
findings.fix: Move the back button fully on-canvas (top 0, left 0 with the chevron inset) and put the tabs on a 32+8 = 40px pitch at ≥28px tall.

findings.what: The equation is a centred compact cluster with double the reference's side margins, so it does not span the header panel the way the reference's does.
findings.evidence: DOM on /#/team/knights: the equation's ink runs x 66.5 → 323.5 inside a frame that spans 16 → 374 — 50px of dead panel on each side. Measuring the reference JPEG, `5.6` starts at x≈130/1080 (≈47 CSS) and `7.6` ends at x≈960/1080 (≈347 CSS) inside a frame spanning ≈20 → 370 CSS — margins of ≈27 and ≈23. The reference reads as an edge-to-edge equation with the total hard right against the frame; the build reads as a centred label.
findings.fix: Justify the equation row (base hard left at the frame's inner margin, total hard right) rather than centring it.

findings.what: Plate brushing renders as regular hard horizontal stripes rather than fine irregular anisotropy.
findings.evidence: At 2.2–3.4× the build plates show evenly spaced light/dark bands at roughly a 5px pitch across the whole face, clearly periodic; in the reference crop at comparable scale the brushing is much finer, lower-contrast and irregular. At 1× the build's banding still reads as faint corrugation on the plate faces.
findings.fix: Halve the stripe contrast and randomise the pitch (or drop to a 1–2px repeating gradient with a noise overlay) so it reads as brushed metal rather than ribbing.
